correctness.rationale: Verified EK Remark 3.4 transcription against full HTML v3: mu=((1/(3(d+2)2^{d+3}))(beta/((d+2)2^{d+2}))^d)^{2^{d+1}}, eps=min{1/Q,mu}, bar-eps=(1/3)(beta/((d+2)2^{d+2}))^d. At d=3: C0=1/(3*5*64)=1/960, C1=5*32=160 exactly. Verified universal lemma Exp_b^0(Y)<=2: minimum-weight singleton {v1} has w(v1)<=1/2 hence minimal (norms {w,1-w}), non-coboundary (norm in (0,1/2] vs {0,1}), and ||delta{v1}||=||Gamma^1({v1})||=2w(v1) by EK Lemma 2.3 Eq 2.5 at k=0,r=1 with factor 2; isolated case gives ratio 0. Applies to pure vertex/edge links of a pure d=3 complex (dim>=1, >=2 vertices), of which at least one exists, forcing admissible beta<=2. Monotone substitution gives eps_bar<=(1/3)(2/160)^3=1/1536000 approx 6.51e-07<0.08 and mu<=((2/160)^3/960)^16=(1/491520000)^16<1e-139<0.08, eps=min{1/Q,mu}<=mu. Recomputed independently in Fractions and replayed output/artifacts/verify_cap.py to VERIFY_OK. Hence no EK output reaches 0.08 at d=3 for any X. Scope honestly limited to published closed form; bare h2>=0.08 by other means not decided. Minor overgenerality for non-pure zero-weight complexes does not affect pure EK application.

Hence the method-specific refutation is new, not a corollary or repackaging of a known stronger fact.

This is not a textbook restatement or mere substitution: it required the universal beta<=2 lemma (minimal singleton plus Lemma 2.3 container identity) combined with monotone EK closed forms, and it corrects Admission feasibility for the method clause. A future researcher attempting an EK certificate at d=3 to 0.08 can cite this to avoid wasted effort and must switch routes (re-optimized constants, Oppenheim descent, Dikstein-Dinur).
